fix(post): Heidenhain DIN/ISO writes the iTNC 530 340 49x cycle 200/205 parameters

The DIN/ISO post wrote Q395 in G200 and Q208/Q395 in G205 for every
control. These words exist only from iTNC 530 60642x-04, TNC 640
34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01 and TNC 320 77185x-01. A small helper now
reads the controller identity: older software gets G200 without Q395 and
G205 without Q208/Q395 (Q379/Q253 stay). A stated control that is not in
the table is refused by name. A machine with no identity keeps the
output of today (decision file).

fix(post): Sinumerik 840D cutting-edge D and a rapid G53 retract

The 840D post wrote `T<n> D<n> M6`. D selects an offset data block of
the active tool (840D sl Fundamentals 12/2018, section 6.6), so tool 12
selected an edge D12 that it does not have. The tool call now writes D1.
A machine file can state `tooling.d_number: "tool-number"` for a control
set to free D numbers with D equal to T.

Each G53 Z retract (setup change, home ask, program end) is now
`G0 G53 Z.. D0`. The program end had no G0, so it moved at the modal
feed or alarmed after G2/G3. G53 suppresses frames only (sections 9.1,
13.10); D0 deselects the tool length (section 6.6), as the manual's own
example `G0 G53 X.. Z.. D0` does (section 4.4). A later section with the
same tool selects its D again before its first move.

Fixes #4143

fix(deburr): start and exit picks for Deburr

The Deburr takes a start point and an exit point (PickCapability::Chain).
The chain nearest the start pick is cut first, from its end nearest the
pick (a closed chain is re-seated at its nearest point). The chain
nearest the exit pick is cut last, to its end nearest the pick. The cut
geometry and the edge breaks stay the automatic ride's; no pick is the
automatic ride byte for byte.

Refused by name before any motion: a pick beyond 1.5 tool diameters of
every chain, an exit at the start end of an open chain, and a plunge or
retract column at a moved chain end that comes within the tool radius
of the part (exact segment-to-facet distance, both moved ends of a
reversed chain).

fix(multiaxis): Rotary Flow refuses a crossing between any two guides

The band loop's meet law read only adjacent guide pairs. A guide that
crossed a guide two or more places away in the pick was machined, and
the bands of the two adjacent pairs folded through the same ground.

A new law (rotary_flow_cross::refuse_crossed_set) reads every
non-adjacent pair of the complete set before the first band is cut,
with a padded box prefilter, and refuses a meet or a crossing by name:
both guides and the crossing point. The adjacent law stays in the band
loop, unchanged.

fix(post): Sodick LN2W TP follows each tapered section's own bottom

The post wrote TP = the post option for each tapered section, but X Y are
on the plane of that section's WireBottom. Two Wire Contour operations of
one setup with different bottom heights got a wrong TP / TN with no
refusal (review of PR #4171).

The option is now tied to one work Z: the WireBottom of the program's
first tapered cut. A later tapered cut gets TP = the option + (its
WireBottom - the first WireBottom) and TN = TP + its height. A TP below
the worktable is refused by name. Each section note names the work Z of
its TP and the work Z that the option states.

Pins: tp_follows_each_tapered_sections_own_bottom,
a_tapered_section_below_the_worktable_is_refused_by_name
(script_sodick_ln2w). The golden edm_test_taper.nc moves in its note
line only.

fix(finish3d): start and exit picks for 3D Finish

The 3D Finish takes a start point and an exit point on its Parallel
pattern, at any pass direction (#3329, slice 2). A pick chooses the
raster corner where the cut starts and where the last pass ends, by
the raster seam's order law of #3330. The cut geometry does not change.

Refused by name, never moved: a pick on another pattern (at the door
and in the generator), a pick far from every corner, an exit that the
start's order cannot end at, a model with no raster pass, a picked
plunge or retract column within the ball radius of the part (exact
segment-to-facet distance), and any later stage that moves a picked
corner (the waterline rings after the raster, the area-control clip):
the finished path is read again.

No pick is the automatic path, byte for byte.

fix(app): the stock export judges the mesh as the file holds it; weld settles duplicates by edge parity

Binary STL writes each corner as f32, so corners closer than one f32 step
are one corner in the file and a mesh that passed the closed check in f64
was written with repeated corners and edges not on two facets.
stock_export::file_bytes rounds to the written values (repair::weld_at_f32);
when a facet collapses there it welds bit-exact and checks the result with
unpaired_edges, refusing by name. A mesh with nothing to collapse writes
byte for byte as before. The UI's stock export and write_stl use it.

repair::drop_degenerate kept one copy of a back-to-back pair, which left its
three edges odd. Duplicates now keep no copy when the rest of the mesh uses
each of their edges an even number of times, and the first copy otherwise
(a stray copy on a closed solid, as pinned before).

fix(sim): the field simulator cuts a move past the per-move ceiling in pieces, so Stock cuts what the column engine cuts

No caller segmented a chord whose swept window passes MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE,
so through Stock the field engine refused ordinary moves: a 12.7 mm
endmill's 300 mm pass, a 127 mm tool's 6 mm plunge, an undercut disc's
6 mm plunge. SdfField::subtract_batch_fitted cuts such a chord or arc
piece as the fewest equal pieces that each pass the ceiling (doubling,
then bisection; it refuses when pieces of one cell still pass it). The
field arms of Stock (simulate_field_with, simulate_undercut, the lathe
and display arms) cut through it; subtract_batch keeps the refusal as
the bound of one update. The #4079 pin moves to subtract_batch directly.

fix(pocket3d): start and exit picks for 3D Pocket

The 3D Pocket takes a start point and an exit point (Region pick).
Each level's first ring starts at its point nearest the start point,
laps back to it and runs on to its old start, so every link stays the
automatic one; zigzag rows start at their nearer end. The last ring
runs on to its point nearest the exit point. The descent goes through
the ladder's entry rule. A start, a descent or an exit beyond reach, an
Adaptive (HSM) level, Adaptive or Rest roughing in the app, and a moved
column within the tool radius of the part (exact clip and
segment-to-facet check) are refused by name. No pick is the old path,
byte for byte.

feat(tools)!: component library store and project persistence

The .camproj file now saves the document tool component table
(components) and each tool's component stack (assembly). The loader
reads the table and every stack before any world write, checks that each
link names a row and that each stack resolves, and lands them through
table_set and set_assembly in place of the clear-on-open. The derived
tool record and body stay as the file states them, so an open never
shifts a posted program.

A document component can link to a user library copy (library_ref: the
library id and an FNV-1a content hash). The user component library is
camcraft-components/1 in CAMCRAFT_COMPONENTS, else
<data dir>/camcraft/components/components.camcomponents, read all or
nothing and saved through a temp file and a rename. The holder library
and the starter catalog are read-only built-in components. sync_status
compares a row with its library copy and never applies it;
SyncDocumentComponent pulls the copy in and derives every user tool
again in one undo step.

The .camtools export of components is left on #3645.

fix(rest): simulate the program ahead in the generation job, not at staging

A rest operation (3D Pocket, Multi-Axis Rough, a rest 2D Pocket or
2D Adaptive) simulated every operation ahead inside collect_job. The
MCP session and the GUI stage a generation on their own thread, so a
long simulation blocked every other call even with the #3860 worker.

fix(sim): weight the B letter by |cos A| in the mid-pose swing bound

The mid-pose walk bounds the axis turn inside an interval by the
letters' sweep, each letter at one radian for each radian. B turns the
axis only |cos A| for each radian. axis_to_angles writes a radial pose
under the A line as B180 and over it as B0, so at A = -90 one pose
flips B by 180. The old bound read that flip as a 90 degree swing. The
posed fixture sweep then grew the spindle housing capsule by hundreds
of mm into the machine table, and the post refused a legal Rotary Flow
on a turning A with "spindle housing at move N strikes a fixture".

The bound now counts B at the largest |cos A| the move holds. It is
still a proven upper bound, so every law that reads the swing keeps
enclosing the true sweep.

fix(multiaxis): prove every swarf exit rise with an exact sweep

The full-band swarf tests failed the release gate with nine RapidInPart
warnings. The nine moves were the plan's own retract rapids off each
side-pass level. The stamp gave each of them the held lying pose with no
proof, and the flank (or, under the tube's equator, the ball) rose
through the blade.

- stamp_sweep.rs: the exact distance from a tool axis swept along a
  straight move (a parallelogram) to each facet, by the
  triangle-triangle distance law.
- stamp_rise.rs: the rise proof uses that sweep instead of r/2 samples,
  against the start pose's own gap. A plan rapid rise answers to the
  same proof. If it is not proved, it leaves along the contact normal
  under the same pose, then rises, each leg proved. If no exit is
  proved, it stays the plan's own and the verifier judges it.
